title: Melt Electrospinning Writing of Three-dimensional Poly(ε-caprolactone) Scaffolds with Controllable Morphologies for Tissue Engineering Applications
protocol: Fill 2 g of PCL into a 3 mL plastic syringe with a funnel.
Insert a piston into the open end of the syringe.
Place the syringe in a preheated oven at 65 °C for 8 h.
Point the tip upwards to allow air bubbles to aggregate near the opening.
Push the piston with a thin object to release trapped air within the molten material.
Let it cool down until the polymer is no longer transparent after 10 minutes.
Store the PCL pre-loaded syringe at room temperature in a dry and dark environment.
Attach a 23G flat tipped needle (spinneret) to the syringe.
Connect the syringe to the air pressure system with a barrel adapter.
Place the syringe in the print head and press it down until the spinneret tip stands out 1 mm from the brass part on the bottom side of the head.
Mount a collector on the stage.
Clean the surface of the collector and the print head with 70% ethanol to remove dust or residual polymer.
Set the working distance by positioning a 12 mm high object between the spinneret and the collector and lower the print head until the spinneret tip just touches it.
Adjust the temperature regulators at the electrical box to 82 °C for the spinneret region and 65 °C for the syringe.
Power on the temperature regulators to melt the PCL.
Wait for at least 10 min until the polymer is molten.
Initiate the air pressure by setting the regulator to 1.8 bar.
Prepare the G-Code to define the size and shape, inter-filament distance, number of layers of the scaffold, and collection speed of the process.
Double-check manually that all ground cables are connected securely to the enclosure and the wall plug.
Start the software (e.g., MACH 3) on the computer and upload the prepared G-code.
Close the front door of the enclosure to connect the safety interlock and trigger the high voltage supply to the spinneret.
Increase the high voltage gradually in 0.2 kV steps until a Taylor cone is formed and a fiber is ejected towards the collector.
Allow the polymer melt to be extruded on the still collector plate to stabilize the jet without movement for 5 minutes.
Remove the pile of material before commencing a new print.
Use the cursors on the keyboard to move the print head above the point where the G-codes will start.
Start the G-Code in the software on the computer.
Keep the working distance at 12 mm.
Maintain the temperature regulator at 82 °C for the spinneret region.
Set the temperature regulator to 65 °C for the syringe.
Reduce the air pressure level to 0.8 bar.
Adjust the applied voltage to 8 kV.
Set the collector speed to 1700 mm/min.
Print fibers with small sized diameters (3-10 µm).
Increase the air pressure level to 1.5 bar.
Set the voltage to 11 kV.
Lower the collection speed to 1200 mm/min.
Print fibers with medium sized diameters (10-20 µm).
Increase the air pressure level to 2.6 bar.
Alter the applied voltage to 12 kV.
Decrease the collection speed to 700 mm/min.
Print fibers with large diameters (20-30 µm).
Illuminate the jet with a strong LED light for improved visibility.
Observe the behavior of the fiber for 1 minute.
Adjust system parameters in small steps: 0.1 kV for applied voltage, 100 mm/min for collection speed, and 0.1 bar for air pressure.
Decrease the air-pressure to stabilize periodically deflecting behavior.
Increase the speed until the flight path of the fiber resembles a stable catenary curve for more than 3 minutes.
Minimize the voltage until the flight path stabilizes.
Increase the voltage to correct the flight path of a lagging behind jet.
Reduce the air pressure to adjust the flight path of the jet.
Reduce the speed of the collector if necessary.
Continue applying measures until the flight path returns to a catenary curve shape.
Decrease the applied voltage to prevent fibers from traveling vertically towards the collector.
Increase the speed of the collector to maintain the correct flight path.
Increase the air pressure to ensure the flight path retains the shape of a catenary curve.
Open the door when the print is finished.
Move the collector plate towards the door using the cursor for better accessibility.
Spray the scaffold with ethanol 70% (vol/vol) mix.
Wait 10 seconds until the scaffold visibly detaches from the collector.
Collect the finished scaffold by grabbing one edge with tweezers.
Lift the scaffold out of the enclosure.
Decrease the applied voltage if a spark between the spinneret is visible or audible.
Open the door immediately upon hearing a cracking noise.
Remove all hazardous materials and liquids such as ethanol 70% (vol/vol) from inside the enclosure to prevent fire ignition.
Program the G-Code accordingly that the spinneret moves away from the printed area after completing all layers.
Check the spinneret under a magnifier.
Verify that there is no damage to the spinneret.
